paragraphs.title: The Psalm’s Heading and the Supplicant’s Prayer

answers: Hear his cry and attend to his prayer
Build him a strong tower
Prolong the king’s life
easy.explanation: The speaker says, “Hear my cry, O God; attend unto my prayer.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask God to do?

answers: To the king
Unto God
To the enemy
easy.explanation: The speaker cries unto God from the end of the earth.
easy.q: To whom does the speaker cry?

answers: A request addressed to God
A royal command
A song of victory
easy.explanation: The speaker asks God to attend unto his prayer, meaning his request or petition.
easy.q: What does the word “prayer” refer to in verse 1?

answers: With a description of a battle
With a musical heading
With a promise to the king
medium.explanation: The psalm begins with the heading, “To the chief Musician upon Neginah, A Psalm of David.”
medium.q: How does the psalm begin according to the KJV passage?

answers: His cry and his prayer
His vows and his inheritance
Mercy and truth
medium.explanation: He says, “Hear my cry” and “attend unto my prayer.”
medium.q: What two things does the speaker ask God to hear or attend to?

answers: A joyful shout at a feast
An earnest call for help
A command to the king
medium.explanation: Here, “cry” means an earnest appeal or call to God for help.
medium.q: What does “cry” most nearly mean in this context?

answers: It introduces a setting connected with singing and prayer
It cancels the speaker’s prayer
It describes the king’s inheritance
challenge.explanation: The musical heading is followed by a direct prayer asking God to hear the speaker.
challenge.q: How does the musical heading relate to the next verse?

answers: From a general cry to a specific request for attention to his prayer
From thanksgiving to a description of battle
From a royal command to a promise of escape
challenge.explanation: The speaker first asks God to hear his cry and then asks Him to attend unto his prayer.
challenge.q: What progression appears in the speaker’s words?

answers: The passage is presented as a personal prayer
The speaker is describing a distant country
The speaker is giving instructions to musicians
challenge.explanation: Addressing God directly shows that the speaker is praying and making a personal appeal.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the direct address, “O God”?

answers: From the end of the earth
From the king’s palace
From the strong tower
easy.explanation: The speaker says, “From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee.”
easy.q: Where does the speaker say he will cry unto God?

answers: The heritage of the fearful
The rock that is higher than he
The king’s throne
easy.explanation: He asks, “lead me to the rock that is higher than I.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask God to lead him to?

answers: As a shelter and a strong tower
As a distant king and judge
As a song and a vow
easy.explanation: The speaker says God has been “a shelter for me, and a strong tower from the enemy.”
easy.q: How is God described in verse 3?

answers: Because his own strength is greater than the rock
Because the rock represents help beyond his own ability
Because he wants to leave God’s shelter
medium.explanation: The higher rock pictures a place of strength and help beyond the speaker’s own ability.
medium.q: Why does the speaker ask God to lead him to a higher rock?

answers: A time of great distress
A time of royal celebration
A time of daily singing
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the speaker’s troubled and burdened condition.
medium.q: What does “when my heart is overwhelmed” describe?

answers: God’s sheltering protection
A hiding place for an enemy
A room in the king’s palace
medium.explanation: The image of being under God’s wings represents safety and protection.
medium.q: What does “the covert of thy wings” suggest?

answers: The speaker needs God’s direction because he is unable to manage the distress alone
The speaker has already solved every difficulty
The speaker is asking to abandon God’s protection
challenge.explanation: Because the speaker is overwhelmed, he asks God to lead him to a rock higher than himself.
challenge.q: What connection exists between the overwhelmed heart and the request for guidance?

answers: The words “for ever” and the request to trust under God’s wings
The mention of the end of the earth alone
The reference to the king’s years
challenge.explanation: Abiding in God’s tabernacle “for ever” and trusting under His wings express continuing protection.
challenge.q: What emphasizes the speaker’s desire for lasting protection?

answers: God has heard his vows and given him an inheritance
God has removed the king from his throne
God has sent a new enemy
challenge.explanation: The speaker says God has heard his vows and given him the heritage of those who fear His name.
challenge.q: What additional blessing does the speaker mention in verse 5?

answers: That the king’s life be prolonged
That the king hide from his people
That the king leave the kingdom
easy.explanation: The speaker asks, “Thou wilt prolong the king’s life.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask concerning the king?

answers: Mercy and truth
The rock and the tower
The song and the inheritance
easy.explanation: He asks for mercy and truth, “which may preserve him.”
easy.q: What does the speaker ask to preserve the king?

answers: Sing praise and perform his vows
Build a tower for the enemy
Travel to the end of the earth
easy.explanation: He promises to sing praise forever and daily perform his vows.
easy.q: What does the speaker promise to do continually?

answers: As lasting only one season
As lasting through many generations
As ending with the speaker’s prayer
medium.explanation: The verse says, “his years as many generations.”
medium.q: How are the king’s years described?

answers: The request for the king’s preservation is followed by praise and vows
The king’s preservation causes the speaker to flee
The request ends with a description of the enemy
medium.explanation: After asking that mercy and truth preserve the king, the speaker promises praise and faithfulness.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the king’s preservation and the speaker’s response?

answers: To fulfill promises made to God
To rule over the king
To hide from danger
medium.explanation: To perform vows means to keep or fulfill promises made before God.

answers: God’s preserving care leads to continuing praise and obedience
The king’s reign leads to a rejection of prayer
The inheritance leads to a new description of the enemy
challenge.explanation: The request for the king to be preserved is followed by the speaker’s commitment to praise God and keep his vows.
challenge.q: What idea connects the king’s preservation with the final verse?

answers: A single act performed once
A repeated and continuing practice
The cancellation of the vows
challenge.explanation: “Daily” shows that the speaker intends to perform his vows continually.

answers: It shifts from a request for the king to the speaker’s personal commitment
It shifts from protection to a description of battle
It shifts from inheritance to the speaker’s distress
challenge.explanation: The passage first concerns the king’s long life and then turns to the speaker’s promise of praise and obedience.
challenge.q: How does the focus shift from the king’s life to the final verse?
